q: Which one of the following statements relating to the official languages of the States and Union Territories is FALSE?

options.A: The official language of the State of Nagaland is English
options.B: The official language of the State of Mizoram is Hindi
options.C: The official language of the State of Goa is Konkani
options.D: The official languages of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands are Hindi and English

e: The official language of Mizoram is Mizo, with English also used for official purposes; it is not Hindi, so statement B is false. Nagaland's official language is English, Goa's is Konkani, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands use Hindi and English.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the chairmanship of the bodies for the Official Language is FALSE?

options.A: The Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister
options.B: The Official Language Implementation Committee (Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) of a Central Government office is chaired by the head of the office
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose
options.D: The Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee of a Railway Division is chaired by the Divisional Railway Manager

e: The Central Official Language Implementation Committee is not chaired by the Prime Minister; it works under the Department of Official Language, so statement A is false. An office Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the head of office, a Town Committee by the nominated senior-most Central Government officer in the town, and a Railway Divisional Committee by the Divisional Railway Manager.

q: A Central Government office finalises certain regulations and proposes to issue them in English only, on the ground that they are meant for official use within the Government. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the regulations are required to be issued in:

options.A: Hindi only
options.B: English only
options.C: Both Hindi and English
options.D: The regional language of the State of location only

e: Regulations are among the documents listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, for which both Hindi and English must be used; regulations must therefore be issued in both languages, not in English only, even if meant for internal official use.

q: A Central Government office prints the forms used in its office work in English only, on the ground that they are filled in by its own staff. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature of Central Government offices are required to be printed and published in:

options.A: Diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English
options.B: Hindi only
options.C: English only
options.D: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English

e: Rule 11 of the Official Languages Rules, 1976 requires manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature of Central Government offices to be printed and published in diglot form, that is, in Hindi and English.

q: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted in a town and it is proposed that its meetings should be chaired by the District Magistrate of the district. The correct position is that the Committee is chaired by:

options.A: The District Magistrate of the district
options.B: The senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose
options.C: The Secretary, Department of Official Language
options.D: The Hindi Officer of the biggest Central Government office in the town

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer, the head of office, in the town who is nominated for the purpose; the District Magistrate, a State officer, does not chair it.

q: At a check point in a Central Government office, a contract covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 is presented for despatch in Hindi only. The correct course of action is:

options.A: To despatch it in Hindi, Hindi being the Official Language of the Union
options.B: To despatch it in Hindi and send the English version a week later
options.C: To translate it into English at the check point and despatch the English version alone
options.D: Not to let the document leave the office unless it is issued in both Hindi and English

e: Contracts are documents covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and must be issued in both Hindi and English; a check point must not let such a document leave the office in Hindi only.

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 62 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award is admissible at this level of marks

e: Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 54 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award is admissible, the lowest slab of the cash award beginning at 55 per cent marks

e:
The lowest slab of cash award for Pragya begins at 55 per cent marks; at 54 per cent the employee passes but earns no cash award.
Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q: An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 89 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 85 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination
options.C: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 90 per cent or more marks
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months

e: A cash award for the Hindi typewriting examination requires 90 per cent or more marks; at 89 per cent the threshold is not reached, so no cash award is admissible.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 25 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 25 words per minute
options.B: He fails, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 30 words per minute
options.C: He passes, the examination being decided on marks alone and not on speed
options.D: He passes only if he also secures 90 per cent marks in the Pragya examination

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is 30 words per minute; a speed of 25 words per minute is below the passing standard, so the candidate fails.

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 86 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 85 per cent or more marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 80 per cent or more marks
options.D: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute

e: The cash award threshold for the Hindi stenography examination is 88 per cent or more marks; at 86 per cent the threshold is not reached, so no cash award is admissible.

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 91 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold of 88 per cent or more marks having been secured
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months

e: At 91 per cent marks in the Hindi stenography examination, the prescribed cash award threshold of 88 per cent or more is crossed, so a cash award is admissible.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 79 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 70 words per minute
options.B: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 75 words per minute
options.C: He fails, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 80 words per minute
options.D: He passes only if he also secures 88 per cent marks in the theory paper

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute; at 79 words per minute the candidate falls just short and fails.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 81 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He fails, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.B: He fails, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.C: He passes only if he also secures 88 per cent marks in the theory paper
options.D: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 80 words per minute

e: Since the prescribed passing speed in the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute, a candidate attaining 81 words per minute passes the examination.

q: An employee aged 37 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: The training is optional for him and he may decline it without assigning any reason
options.B: The training is compulsory for him, the exemption from compulsory training applying only on attaining the age of 45 years
options.C: The nomination is not in order, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory below the age of 45 years
options.D: He can be nominated only for the correspondence course conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate

e: Compulsory in-service Hindi training applies to employees who lack working knowledge of Hindi, and exemption applies only on attaining 45 years of age; a 37-year-old employee is therefore under compulsory training.

q: An employee aged 49 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for compulsory in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: The training is compulsory for him at every age
options.B: He can be compelled to undergo the training only during the last year of his service
options.C: The training is not compulsory for him, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years
options.D: He can be nominated only with the prior approval of the Department of Official Language

e: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years; a 49-year-old employee therefore cannot be compelled to undergo it.

q: In a Central Government office, 78 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion of 80 per cent or more of the staff not having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 75 per cent or more of the staff
options.C: The office can be notified with the special approval of the Department of Official Language
options.D: The office stands automatically notified on crossing 75 per cent of the staff

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; at 78 per cent the proportion is short, so the office cannot be notified.

q: In a Central Government office, 87 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 100 per cent of the staff
options.B: The office cannot be notified, notification requiring 90 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: The office stands automatically notified without any notification in the Official Gazette
options.D: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion of 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi

e: At 87 per cent, the staff with working knowledge of Hindi exceeds the 80 per cent proportion prescribed for notification under Rule 10(4) of the Official Languages Rules, 1976, so the office can be notified in the Official Gazette.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 17,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 20,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
options.C: He is eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum of 10,000 words in a year having been exceeded
options.D: He is not eligible for consideration, the scheme applying only to noting done in Region 'A' offices

e: The incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi requires a minimum of 10,000 words in a year; 17,000 words exceeds it, so the employee is eligible for consideration for a cash award, irrespective of Region or notification of the office.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the ninth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: Personal pay is admissible in the ninth month only at half the rate of one increment
options.B: Personal pay is admissible in the ninth month only if he has passed the next higher Hindi examination in the meantime
options.C: Personal pay is not admissible in the ninth month, its total period of admissibility being 6 months
options.D: Personal pay continues to be admissible in the ninth month, its total period of admissibility being 12 months

e: Personal pay equal to one increment, granted on passing the prescribed Hindi examination, is admissible for a total of 12 months; it therefore continues to be admissible in the ninth month.

q: A town has nine Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town:

options.A: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, the town having five or more Central Government offices
options.B: No Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted, such a committee requiring ten or more Central Government offices in the town
options.C: The implementation work is to be looked after directly by the Department of Official Language
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted only if all the offices are headed by Hindi-knowing officers

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee requires ten or more Central Government offices in the town; with only nine offices the condition is not met, so no such committee can be constituted.

q: A town has eleven Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town:

options.A: No Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted, such a committee requiring twenty or more Central Government offices in the town
options.B: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted only if all the offices are headed by Hindi-knowing officers
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, the town having ten or more Central Government offices
options.D: The implementation work is to be looked after directly by the Department of Official Language

e: With eleven Central Government offices, the town crosses the minimum of ten offices prescribed for constituting a Town Official Language Implementation Committee, so such a committee is to be constituted there.

q: A Central Government office spends 49 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for purchase of books. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, at least 40 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.B: The claim is in order, at least 25 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.C: The claim is in order only if the office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: The claim is not in order, at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries being required to be spent on Hindi books

e: The Annual Programme target is that at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on books for office libraries be spent on Hindi books; spending only 49 per cent falls short, so the claim of compliance is not in order.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'A' originates 98 per cent of its correspondence in Hindi and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for Hindi correspondence. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is not in order, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Region 'A' being 100 per cent
options.B: The claim is in order, the target for offices located in Region 'A' being 90 per cent
options.C: The claim is in order, the target for offices located in Region 'A' being 75 per cent
options.D: The claim is in order only if the remaining correspondence was issued bilingually

e: The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region A offices is 100 per cent; originating 98 per cent in Hindi leaves a shortfall, so the claim of compliance is not in order.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' originates 92 per cent of its correspondence in Hindi and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for Hindi correspondence. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is not in order, the target for offices located in Region 'B' being 100 per cent
options.B: The claim is in order, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Region 'B' being 90 per cent
options.C: The claim is not in order, the target for offices located in Region 'B' being 95 per cent
options.D: The claim is in order only if the office has been notified under Rule 10(4)

e: The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region B offices is 90 per cent; an office originating 92 per cent in Hindi meets that target, so its claim is in order.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under clause (2) of Article 343 of the Constitution, during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, the President could, by order, authorise the use of Hindi in addition to English, and of the Devanagari form of numerals in addition to the international form of Indian numerals, for any of the official purposes of the Union.
2. The Hindi Teaching Scheme for imparting in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees was introduced in the year 1955.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Article 343(2) allowed the President, during the first fifteen years, to authorise by order the use of Hindi in addition to English, and of Devanagari numerals in addition to the international form of Indian numerals, for official purposes of the Union. The Hindi Teaching Scheme for in-service training began in 1955, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 3(1) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, notwithstanding the expiration of the period of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, English may continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for all the official purposes of the Union for which it was in use and for the transaction of business in Parliament.
2. Arabic became one of the official languages of the United Nations in the year 1973.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Section 3(1) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides that, notwithstanding the expiry of fifteen years, English shall continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for the official purposes of the Union and for business in Parliament. Arabic became an official language of the United Nations in 1973, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 29 of the Constitution, any section of the citizens residing in India having a distinct language, script or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same.
2. Bihar was the first province in India to adopt Hindi in the Devanagari script in place of Persian for court work, in the year 1881.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Article 29(1) gives any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture of its own the right to conserve it. Bihar was the first province to adopt Hindi in the Devanagari script in place of Persian for court work, in 1881, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. Bengali is the second most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India.
2. The Sahitya Akademi, India's national academy of letters, was established in the year 1954.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: As per the Census of India, 2011, Bengali is the second most widely spoken mother tongue in India, after Hindi. The Sahitya Akademi, India's national academy of letters, was established in 1954, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At present, the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution contains 22 languages.
2. English is one of the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Eighth Schedule at present contains 22 languages, following additions by the 21st, 71st, 92nd and other amendments. English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule, so statement 1 alone is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sanskrit was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2005.
2. Telugu was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2008.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Sanskrit was accorded classical language status in 2005, following Tamil in 2004, and Telugu was accorded that status in 2008, along with Kannada; both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sixth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1999 at London.
2. The Fifth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1996 at Johannesburg (South Africa).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 1 only

e: The Sixth World Hindi Conference was held at London in 1999. The Fifth World Hindi Conference, in 1996, was held at Port of Spain in Trinidad and Tobago, not at Johannesburg, so statement 2 is wrong and statement 1 alone is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Jharkhand is placed in Region 'A'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Odisha is placed in Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Jharkhand is placed in Region A and Odisha in Region C under the Official Languages Rules, 1976, Odisha being grouped with the non-Hindi States of the east and south for correspondence purposes; both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Mizoram is Hindi.
2. The official language of the State of Meghalaya is English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The official language of Mizoram is Mizo, not Hindi, so statement 1 is wrong. The official language of Meghalaya is English, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Institute of Indian Languages, headquartered at Mysuru, was established in the year 1969.
2. The Central Hindi Directorate was established in the year 1971.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Central Institute of Indian Languages, headquartered at Mysuru, was established in 1969. The Central Hindi Directorate was established in 1960, not 1971, so statement 1 alone is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar and the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language are presented every year on the occasion of Hindi Diwas (14th September).
2. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded on Indian Railways to the Division adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 1 only

e: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar and Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language are presented every year on Hindi Diwas, 14 September. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield goes to the best Zonal Railway, not to a Division, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The secretariat of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is provided by the Department of Official Language.
2. The Committee of Parliament on Official Language discharges its functions through three sub-committees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The secretariat of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is provided by the Department of Official Language, and the Committee discharges its functions through three sub-committees which inspect offices and study evidence; both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee of a Railway Division is chaired by the Divisional Railway Manager.
2. The Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office normally holds its meetings twice a year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee of a Railway Division is chaired by the Divisional Railway Manager. An office Official Language Implementation Committee is required to meet quarterly, not twice a year, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Punjab is placed in Region 'A'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Karnataka is placed in Region 'B'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Punjab is placed in Region B, not Region A, and Karnataka is placed in Region C, not Region B, under the Official Languages Rules, 1976; neither statement is correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 4 from Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Section 4 provides that the Hindi translation of a Central Act shall be deemed to be its authoritative text in Hindi, while Section 5 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.B: Section 4 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 5 provides that a translation in Hindi of any Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi
options.C: Both the Sections deal only with the use of Hindi for judgments, decrees or orders of the High Courts
options.D: Section 4 vests the rule-making power in the Central Government, while Section 5 deals with the authoritative Hindi text of State Acts

e: Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides for the Committee of Parliament on Official Language to review the progress of Hindi. Section 5 provides that a Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed its authoritative text in Hindi.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 347 from Article 350 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 347 entitles every person to submit a representation for the redress of a grievance, while Article 350 empowers the President to direct the recognition of a language
options.B: Both the Articles deal only with instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
options.C: Article 347 deals with the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts, while Article 350 deals with the development of Hindi
options.D: Article 347 empowers the President to direct that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall also be officially recognised for specified purposes, while Article 350 entitles every person to submit a representation for the redress of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be

e: Article 347 empowers the President to direct official recognition of a language spoken by a substantial proportion of a State's population for specified purposes. Article 350 entitles every person to submit a representation for redress of a grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any language used in the Union or that State.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Praveen course from the Parangat course under the Hindi Teaching Scheme?

options.A: Praveen corresponds broadly to the middle (Class VIII) level and is undergone after Prabodh, while Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work
options.B: Praveen is the final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff, while Parangat is the first prescribed course for beginners
options.C: Both the courses correspond broadly to the Matriculation (Class X) level
options.D: Praveen is a course in Hindi stenography, while Parangat is a course in Hindi typewriting

e: Praveen, taken after Prabodh, corresponds broadly to the middle, Class VIII, level. Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who need advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work, so statement A correctly distinguishes the two.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Central Translation Bureau from the Official Language Wing (Rajbhasha Khand) of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice?

options.A: The Central Translation Bureau prepares the Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts, while the Official Language Wing translates codes, manuals and forms
options.B: Both the bodies conduct the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.C: The Central Translation Bureau is mainly responsible for the translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices, while the Official Language Wing of the Legislative Department prepares the Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts
options.D: Both the bodies function only at the level of Zonal Railways

e: The Central Translation Bureau translates codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices. The Official Language Wing of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, prepares the Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts, so statement C is correct.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the institutions for the Official Language is FALSE?

options.A: The Department of Official Language functions in the Ministry of Home Affairs
options.B: The Central Hindi Directorate functions under the Ministry of Education
options.C: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi), Agra functions under the Ministry of Education
options.D: The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi functions under the Ministry of Education

e: The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi, functions under the Department of Official Language in the Ministry of Home Affairs, not under the Ministry of Education, so statement D is false; the other three institutional locations are correctly stated.

q: Which one of the following statements about the year in which the status of a 'classical language' was conferred on Indian languages is FALSE?

options.A: Tamil was accorded the status of a 'classical language' in the year 2004
options.B: Sanskrit was accorded the status of a 'classical language' in the year 2005
options.C: Marathi was accorded the status of a 'classical language' in the year 2013
options.D: Odia was accorded the status of a 'classical language' in the year 2014

e: Marathi was accorded classical language status in 2024, not 2013, so statement C is false. Tamil in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005 and Odia in 2014 are correctly stated; the 2013 addition was Malayalam.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the official languages of the States is FALSE?

options.A: The official language of the State of Haryana is Punjabi
options.B: The official language of the State of Himachal Pradesh is Hindi
options.C: The official language of the State of Goa is Konkani
options.D: The official language of the State of Nagaland is English

e: The official language of Haryana is Hindi, not Punjabi, although Punjabi has the status of a second official language there, so statement A is false. Himachal Pradesh has Hindi, Goa has Konkani, and Nagaland has English as official language.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the additions to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is FALSE?

options.A: Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (21st Amendment) Act, 1967
options.B: Bodo was added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992
options.C: Dogri was added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003
options.D: By the Constitution (96th Amendment) Act, 2011, the name 'Oriya' in the Eighth Schedule was replaced by 'Odia'

e: Bodo was added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003, along with Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, not by the 71st Amendment of 1992, which added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; hence statement B is false, while the Sindhi, Dogri and Odia statements are correct.

q: At a check point in a Central Government office, a licence (permit) covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 is presented for despatch in Hindi only. The correct course of action is:

options.A: To despatch it in Hindi, Hindi being the Official Language of the Union
options.B: Not to let the document leave the office unless it is issued in both Hindi and English
options.C: To despatch it in Hindi and send the English version a week later
options.D: To translate it into English at the check point and despatch the English version alone

e: Licences and permits are among the documents covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, which must be issued in both Hindi and English; the check point must not let the licence leave the office in Hindi only.

q: A Central Government office sends an ordinary communication in Hindi to an office of a State Government located in Region 'B', without enclosing any English translation. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The communication is in order, an English translation being required to accompany a communication issued in Hindi only when it is addressed to an office located in Region 'C'
options.B: The communication must be accompanied by its English translation in every case
options.C: The communication must be accompanied by its translation in the regional language of that State
options.D: The communication is in order only with the prior approval of the Department of Official Language

e: Under Rule 5 of the Official Languages Rules, 1976, an English translation must accompany a Hindi communication only when it is addressed to an office or person in Region C; for a Region B office a communication in Hindi is in order without an English translation.

q: In a Central Government office which has NOT been notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi is directed to do all his noting and drafting in Hindi only. The correct position is:

options.A: The direction is in order, every employee with working knowledge of Hindi being bound to work only in Hindi
options.B: The direction is in order only during Hindi Pakhwada
options.C: The direction is not in order, an employee in such an office being free to make noting and drafting in Hindi or in English, as he may choose
options.D: The direction is in order only if issued in writing by the Department of Official Language

e: In an office not notified under Rule 10(4), an employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi is free to make noting and drafting in Hindi or in English, as he chooses; a direction to work in Hindi only is therefore not in order in such an office.

q: A Central Government office displays its sign board in Hindi and English only, the regional language of the area being omitted altogether. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that sign boards of Central Government offices are required to be displayed in:

options.A: Hindi and English only, as displayed by the office
options.B: Hindi only
options.C: The regional language and English only
options.D: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English

e: Sign boards of Central Government offices are displayed in three languages - the regional language, Hindi and English - in that order of precedence practice, so omitting the regional language makes the display defective.

q: A member of the public residing in Region 'A' submits an application to a Central Government office in English. The office refuses to accept it, saying that applications are accepted only in Hindi. The correct position under the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office is right, applications in Region 'A' being accepted in Hindi only
options.B: The office is wrong, a member of the public being free to submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or in English
options.C: The application should have been submitted in the regional language of the State
options.D: The application can be accepted only with the approval of the head of the office

e: Under the Official Languages Rules, 1976, a member of the public may submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or in English; an office in Region A cannot refuse an application merely because it is in English.

q: An office has been notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976. The head of the office directs an employee who has NOT acquired working knowledge of Hindi to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification. The correct position is:

options.A: The direction is in order, the notification binding every employee of the office alike
options.B: The direction is in order only during Hindi Pakhwada
options.C: The direction is not in order, the requirement to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the specified subjects applying to employees who have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The direction is in order only if the employee has passed the Prabodh examination

e: In an office notified under Rule 10(4), the obligation to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification applies only to employees who have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; it cannot be imposed on an employee who has not acquired such knowledge.

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 76 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award is admissible at this level of marks

e: Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 52 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award is admissible, the lowest slab of the cash award beginning at 55 per cent marks

e:
Cash awards for Pragya begin at 55 per cent marks; at 52 per cent the employee is below the lowest slab, so no cash award is admissible.
Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q: An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 88 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 90 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 85 per cent or more marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 80 per cent or more marks
options.D: A cash award is admissible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination

e: The cash award threshold for the Hindi typewriting examination is 90 per cent or more marks; at 88 per cent the threshold is not reached, so no cash award is admissible.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 32 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He fails, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 40 words per minute
options.B: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 30 words per minute
options.C: He fails, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 35 words per minute
options.D: He passes only if he also secures 90 per cent marks in the Pragya examination

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is 30 words per minute; a candidate attaining 32 words per minute therefore passes.

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 94 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months
options.D: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold of 88 per cent or more marks having been secured

e: At 94 per cent marks in the Hindi stenography examination, the cash award threshold of 88 per cent or more is comfortably crossed, so a cash award is admissible.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 88 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 80 words per minute
options.B: He fails, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.C: He fails, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.D: He passes only if he also secures 88 per cent marks in the theory paper

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute; a candidate attaining 88 words per minute therefore passes.

q: An employee aged 36 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: The training is optional for him and he may decline it without assigning any reason
options.B: The nomination is not in order, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory below the age of 45 years
options.C: He can be nominated only for the correspondence course conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate
options.D: The training is compulsory for him, the exemption from compulsory training applying only on attaining the age of 45 years

e: Compulsory in-service Hindi training applies until an employee attains 45 years of age; a 36-year-old employee lacking working knowledge of Hindi is therefore under compulsory training, the exemption applying only on attaining 45.

q: An employee aged 50 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for compulsory in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: The training is compulsory for him at every age
options.B: The training is not compulsory for him, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years
options.C: He can be compelled to undergo the training only during the last year of his service
options.D: He can be nominated only with the prior approval of the Department of Official Language

e: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years; a 50-year-old employee therefore cannot be compelled to undergo compulsory training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme.

q: In a Central Government office, 91 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion of 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 100 per cent of the staff
options.C: The office cannot be notified, notification requiring 95 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The office stands automatically notified without any notification in the Official Gazette

e: At 91 per cent, the proportion of staff with working knowledge of Hindi exceeds the 80 per cent prescribed for notification under Rule 10(4) of the Official Languages Rules, 1976, so the office can be notified; notification is by gazette notification, not automatic.

q: In a Central Government office, 72 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 70 per cent or more of the staff
options.B: The office can be notified with the special approval of the Department of Official Language
options.C: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion of 80 per cent or more of the staff not having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The office stands automatically notified on crossing 70 per cent of the staff

e: Notification under Rule 10(4) requires 80 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; at 72 per cent the office cannot be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 19,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 20,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum of 10,000 words in a year having been exceeded
options.C: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
options.D: He is not eligible for consideration, the scheme applying only to noting done in Region 'A' offices

e: The incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi requires a minimum of 10,000 words in a year; 19,000 words exceeds that minimum, so the employee is eligible for consideration for a cash award.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 8,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 5,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if he repeats the performance in the following year
options.C: He is eligible for consideration only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year

e: With only 8,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year, the employee falls short of the minimum of 10,000 words prescribed under the incentive scheme, so he is not eligible for consideration.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the fourth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: Personal pay continues to be admissible in the fourth month, its total period of admissibility being 12 months
options.B: Personal pay is admissible in the fourth month only at half the rate of one increment
options.C: Personal pay is not admissible in the fourth month, its total period of admissibility being 3 months
options.D: Personal pay is admissible in the fourth month only if he has passed the next higher Hindi examination in the meantime

e: Personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination is admissible for a total period of 12 months; it therefore continues to be admissible in the fourth month.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the twentieth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: Personal pay continues to be admissible, its total period of admissibility being 24 months
options.B: Personal pay is admissible in the twentieth month only at half the rate of one increment
options.C: Personal pay is not admissible in the twentieth month, its total period of admissibility being 12 months
options.D: Personal pay is admissible in the twentieth month only if he has passed the next higher Hindi examination in the meantime

e: Personal pay equal to one increment is admissible for 12 months only on passing the prescribed Hindi examination; it is not admissible in the twentieth month, and its period is not 24 months.

q: A town has thirteen Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town:

options.A: No Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted, such a committee requiring twenty or more Central Government offices in the town
options.B: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted only if all the offices are headed by Hindi-knowing officers
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, the town having ten or more Central Government offices
options.D: The implementation work is to be looked after directly by the Department of Official Language

e: With thirteen Central Government offices, the town exceeds the minimum of ten offices required for a Town Official Language Implementation Committee, so such a committee is to be constituted there.

q: A Central Government office spends 47 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for purchase of books. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, at least 40 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.B: The claim is in order, at least 25 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.C: The claim is in order only if the office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: The claim is not in order, at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries being required to be spent on Hindi books

e: The Annual Programme target requires at least 50 per cent of the library book purchase amount to be spent on Hindi books; spending only 47 per cent falls short, so the claim of compliance is not in order.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' originates 84 per cent of its correspondence in Hindi and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for Hindi correspondence. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, the target for offices located in Region 'B' being 75 per cent
options.B: The claim is in order, the target for offices located in Region 'B' being 55 per cent
options.C: The claim is in order only if the remaining correspondence was issued bilingually
options.D: The claim is not in order, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Region 'B' being 90 per cent

e: The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region B offices is 90 per cent; originating only 84 per cent in Hindi does not meet the target, so the claim is not in order.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sindhi language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is written in both the Perso-Arabic script and the Devanagari script.
2. The Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya (Mahatma Gandhi International Hindi University) is located at Wardha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Sindhi is written in both the Perso-Arabic script and the Devanagari script, and both are in recognised use. The Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya, the Mahatma Gandhi International Hindi University, is located at Wardha in Maharashtra, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Tripitaka, the canonical literature of Buddhism, is written in the Pali language.
2. 'Ashtadhyayi', the celebrated treatise on Sanskrit grammar, was composed by Panini.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Tripitaka, the canonical literature of Buddhism, is in the Pali language, and the Ashtadhyayi, the celebrated Sanskrit grammar treatise, was composed by Panini; both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. The number of persons who returned Hindi as their mother tongue was approximately 52.8 crore.
2. Urdu is the seventh most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: 1 only

e: As per the Census of India, 2011, about 52.8 crore persons returned Hindi as their mother tongue, the largest number for any language in India. Urdu ranks seventh among mother tongues by number of speakers in that Census, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Usne Kaha Tha', the celebrated Hindi short story, was written by Chandradhar Sharma Guleri.
2. 'Eidgah', the celebrated Hindi short story, was written by Munshi Premchand.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Usne Kaha Tha, the celebrated Hindi short story, was written by Chandradhar Sharma Guleri, and Eidgah was written by Munshi Premchand; both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kanauji dialect belongs to the Eastern Hindi group of dialects.
2. The Magahi language belongs to the Bihari group of languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Kanauji belongs to the Western Hindi group of dialects, not the Eastern Hindi group, so statement 1 is wrong. Magahi belongs to the Bihari group of languages, along with Bhojpuri and Maithili, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Devanagari script, in which Hindi is written, has evolved from the ancient Brahmi script.
2. The Kharoshthi script, used in ancient India, was written from right to left.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 2 only

e: Devanagari, the script of Hindi, evolved through the Gupta and Nagari stages from the ancient Brahmi script. The Kharoshthi script used in ancient north-western India was written from right to left, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, if a communication from a Central Government office to an office or person in Region 'A' is issued in English, it must be accompanied by its Hindi translation.
2. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or in English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the Official Languages Rules, 1976, if a communication to an office or person in Region A is issued in English, its Hindi translation must accompany it. Communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or in English, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rabindranath Tagore's 'Gitanjali' was originally written in the Bengali language.
2. The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Hans' was founded by Munshi Premchand.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Rabindranath Tagore's Gitanjali was originally written in Bengali, and the celebrated Hindi magazine Hans was founded by Munshi Premchand in 1930; both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, the authoritative texts of all orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or the Legislature of a State shall be in the English language.
2. The Gazette of India is published in both Hindi and English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Article 348(1) provides that the authoritative texts of all orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or a State Legislature shall be in English. The Gazette of India is published in both Hindi and English, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi may make noting and drafting on files in Hindi or in English.
2. The Annual Assessment Report on the implementation of the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, which is laid before both Houses of Parliament, is prepared by the Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: An employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi may make noting and drafting on files in Hindi or in English under the Official Languages Rules, 1976. The Annual Assessment Report on implementation of the Annual Programme, laid before both Houses of Parliament, is prepared by the Department of Official Language, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pragya is the first prescribed course under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, meant for employees who do not possess any knowledge of Hindi.
2. Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Pragya is not the first course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme; Prabodh is the first course for beginners, so statement 1 is wrong. Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff needing advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A letter received in Hindi by a Central Government office must be replied to in Hindi, the target for such replies being 100 per cent.
2. The responsibility for ensuring that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are issued in both Hindi and English rests with the officer signing the document.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Letters received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, the target for such replies being 100 per cent. Under the Official Languages Rules, 1976, the responsibility for ensuring that Section 3(3) documents are issued in both Hindi and English rests with the officer signing the document, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the headquarters of a Zonal Railway, the work relating to the implementation of the Official Language Policy is looked after by the Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari (Chief Official Language Officer).
2. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded on Indian Railways to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: At the headquarters of a Zonal Railway, Official Language implementation work is looked after by the Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari, the Chief Official Language Officer. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in Official Language implementation, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi Pakhwada (Hindi Fortnight) is observed every year in Central Government offices and Railways from 14th September to 28th September.
2. The Official Languages (Amendment) Act, 1967 gave statutory effect to the assurance, originally given by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, that English would continue to be used as long as the non-Hindi speaking people required it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Hindi Pakhwada is observed every year in Central Government offices and on the Railways from 14 September to 28 September, beginning with Hindi Diwas. The Official Languages (Amendment) Act, 1967 gave statutory effect to Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru's assurance that English would continue as long as non-Hindi speaking people required it, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the rule for communications to Region 'B' from the rule for communications to Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules, 1976?

options.A: Communications to a State Government office in Region 'B' shall be in English, while those to Region 'C' shall ordinarily be in Hindi
options.B: Communications to both Region 'B' and Region 'C' shall be in the regional language of the State concerned
options.C: Communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region 'B' shall ordinarily be in Hindi, while a communication to a State Government office located in Region 'C' shall be issued in English
options.D: Communications to both Region 'B' and Region 'C' must invariably be accompanied by a translation in the regional language

e: Under Rule 5 of the Official Languages Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region B shall ordinarily be in Hindi, while a communication to a State Government office in Region C shall be in English; this is the correct distinction.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a 'cash award' from 'personal pay' under the incentive schemes relating to the Hindi examinations?

options.A: A cash award is admissible for a period of 12 months, while personal pay is a one-time payment made on the slab basis of marks secured
options.B: A cash award is admissible only on passing the examination through self-study, while personal pay is admissible on the slab basis of marks secured in the examination
options.C: There is no difference between the two; both are equal to one increment and admissible for 12 months
options.D: A cash award is admissible on the slab basis prescribed with reference to the marks secured in a prescribed Hindi, Hindi typewriting or Hindi stenography examination, while personal pay, equal to one increment, is admissible to an employee on passing the prescribed Hindi examination for a period of 12 months

e: A cash award is given on the slab basis prescribed according to the marks secured in a prescribed Hindi, Hindi typewriting or Hindi stenography examination. Personal pay, equal to one increment, is given on passing the prescribed Hindi examination and is admissible for a period of 12 months, so statement D correctly distinguishes them.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar from the Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield?

options.A: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects, while the Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded on Indian Railways to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.B: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is awarded to the best Division in Region 'C', while the Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded for original book writing in Hindi
options.C: Both the awards are given for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects
options.D: Both the awards are given only to individual employees for passing the Pragya examination

e: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is a Railway award given to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in implementation of the Official Language Policy, so statement A is correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes communications between Central Government Ministries from communications sent by a Ministry to its attached and subordinate offices in Region 'A', under the Official Language Rules, 1976?

options.A: Communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another shall be in Hindi only, while those to attached and subordinate offices in Region 'A' may be in Hindi or in English
options.B: Communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or in English, while communications from a Ministry or Department to its attached and subordinate offices situated in Region 'A' shall be in Hindi in such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time
options.C: Both kinds of communications shall invariably be in Hindi, without any exception
options.D: Both kinds of communications shall be in the regional language of the State in which the offices are situated

e: Communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or in English. Communications from a Ministry or Department to its attached and subordinate offices in Region A shall be in Hindi in such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time, as provided in the Official Languages Rules, 1976.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes a Hindi workshop (Hindi Karyashala) from Hindi Pakhwada?

options.A: A Hindi workshop is a fortnight-long observance, while Hindi Pakhwada is a one-day practical training programme
options.B: A Hindi workshop is organised only for employees who have already passed the Pragya examination, while Hindi Pakhwada is organised only for beginners
options.C: A Hindi workshop is organised primarily to give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi, while Hindi Pakhwada is a fortnight-long observance during which programmes such as Hindi essay, noting-and-drafting and elocution competitions are organised
options.D: There is no difference between the two; both are organised only on 14th September

e: A Hindi workshop gives employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi. Hindi Pakhwada is a fortnight-long observance from 14 to 28 September during which programmes such as Hindi essay, noting-and-drafting and elocution competitions are organised, so statement C is correct.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to communications under the Official Language Rules, 1976 is FALSE?

options.A: A communication from a Central Government office to a State Government office located in Region 'C' shall be issued in English
options.B: Communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region 'B' shall ordinarily be in Hindi
options.C: Communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or in English
options.D: If a communication from a Central Government office to an office or person in Region 'A' is issued in English, no Hindi translation is required to accompany it

e: If a communication from a Central Government office to an office or person in Region A is issued in English, its Hindi translation must accompany it under the Official Languages Rules, 1976; the statement that no Hindi translation is required is therefore false, while the Region B, Region C and inter-Ministry statements are correct.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution as originally enacted is FALSE?

options.A: Konkani was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution as originally enacted
options.B: Assamese was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution as originally enacted
options.C: Sanskrit was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution as originally enacted
options.D: Urdu was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution as originally enacted

e: Konkani was not in the Eighth Schedule as originally enacted; it was added by the 71st Amendment in 1992, so statement A is false. Assamese, Sanskrit and Urdu were among the fourteen languages in the Eighth Schedule as originally enacted.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the Rajbhasha awards is FALSE?

options.A: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded on Indian Railways to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.B: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.C: The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy in Regions 'A' and 'B'
options.D: The Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy in Region 'C'

e: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar is for original Hindi book writing on specified subjects, not for the best Zonal Railway, so statement B is false. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is for the best Zonal Railway, the Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield for the best Division in Regions A and B, and the Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield for the best Division in Region C.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the standard of the courses under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is FALSE?

options.A: The standard of the Prabodh course corresponds broadly to the primary (Class V) level
options.B: The standard of the Praveen course corresponds broadly to the middle (Class VIII) level
options.C: The standard of the Parangat course corresponds broadly to the primary (Class V) level
options.D: The standard of the Pragya course corresponds broadly to the matriculation (Class X) level

e: Parangat is an advanced course beyond Pragya and does not correspond to the primary, Class V, level, so statement C is false. Prabodh corresponds broadly to Class V, Praveen to Class VIII and Pragya to Class X, the matriculation level.

q: A Central Government office wishes to release an advertisement in newspapers and proposes to release it in English newspapers only. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that the advertisement should be released:

options.A: In English newspapers only, as advertisements are meant for the educated public
options.B: In Hindi newspapers only
options.C: In the regional language newspapers only
options.D: In Hindi and English (bilingual), i.e., in both Hindi and English newspapers

e: Advertisements of Central Government offices are to be released bilingually, that is, in both Hindi and English newspapers, so that the information reaches both readerships; releasing an advertisement in English newspapers only is contrary to the Official Language Policy.

q: A Central Government office issues a notice inviting applications from the public in English only, on the ground that the applicants are expected to know English. The correct position is that such a notice is required to be issued in both Hindi and English under:

options.A: Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: Article 351 of the Constitution
options.C: The Annual Programme only, and not under any statute
options.D: Article 120 of the Constitution

e: Notices inviting applications, along with tender notices, licences, permits and similar items, are covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, and must be issued in both Hindi and English; the statutory basis is that section, not Article 351 or Article 120.

q: A Ministry of the Central Government directs that every communication sent by it to its attached and subordinate offices situated in Region 'A' must be in Hindi in every case, without any exception. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is that such communications shall be in Hindi:

options.A: Only when the subordinate office demands it in writing
options.B: In such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time
options.C: Only during Hindi Pakhwada
options.D: In every case, without any exception, as directed by the Ministry

e: Under the Official Languages Rules, 1976, communications from a Ministry to its attached and subordinate offices situated in Region A shall be in Hindi in such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time; an inflexible direction for Hindi in every case goes beyond the rule.

q: For working out the percentage of Hindi correspondence of an office in its Quarterly Progress Report, the office counts every letter of which a Hindi translation was prepared, whether or not the letter was originally written in Hindi. The correct position is that, for this purpose, letters are counted as Hindi correspondence only when they are:

options.A: Signed by an officer who knows Hindi
options.B: Typed on a computer in a Hindi font
options.C: Originally written in Hindi
options.D: Addressed to offices located in Region 'A'

e: For the Quarterly Progress Report, correspondence counts as Hindi correspondence only when the letter was originally written in Hindi; a letter originally written in English does not become Hindi correspondence merely because a Hindi translation was later prepared.

q: A resident of Maharashtra submits a representation for the redress of his grievance to a Central Government office in Marathi, a language used in that State. The office returns it, saying that representations are entertained only in Hindi or in English. The correct position under Article 350 of the Constitution is:

options.A: The office is right, a representation being entertainable only in Hindi
options.B: The office is right, a representation being entertainable only in English
options.C: The representation should have been submitted in the Devanagari script alone
options.D: The office is wrong, every person being entitled to submit a representation for the redress of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be

e: Article 350 entitles every person to submit a representation for the redress of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State; a representation in Marathi, a language used in Maharashtra, cannot be returned on the ground that only Hindi or English is accepted.

q: An employee declines to attend a Hindi workshop (Hindi Karyashala) organised in his office, saying that such workshops are meant only to coach employees for the Pragya examination. The correct position is that Hindi workshops are organised primarily to:

options.A: Give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi
options.B: Teach Hindi literature to the staff
options.C: Prepare the staff only for the Pragya examination
options.D: Celebrate Hindi Diwas in the office

e: Hindi workshops are organised primarily to give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi, building on their working knowledge; they are not merely coaching classes for the Pragya examination.

q: An employee has passed the Prabodh examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. His office enrols him for the Prabodh course again, for revision, before allowing him to take the next course. The correct position is that, after passing Prabodh, the employee is required to undergo, as the next course:

options.A: Parangat
options.B: Praveen
options.C: Prabodh itself, once again
options.D: The Hindi stenography course

e: The prescribed sequence under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is Prabodh, then Praveen, then Pragya; after passing Prabodh, the employee must therefore undergo Praveen as the next course, not Prabodh again or Parangat.
